core_idea: Residualize outcome and treatment, then fit a structured final CATE model.
expected_strength: Good when effect heterogeneity is fairly smooth or well represented by chosen features.

core_idea: Use forest splits to learn nonlinear heterogeneous effects with orthogonalization.
expected_strength: Good for nonlinear heterogeneity and segment discovery.

core_idea: Combine outcome and propensity nuisance models into a pseudo-outcome for CATE learning.
expected_strength: Good when either propensity or outcome modeling is strong enough to stabilize estimates.

core_idea: Fit one outcome model using treatment as a feature, then contrast predicted outcomes.
expected_strength: Simple baseline that can work when treatment interactions are learned well.

core_idea: Fit separate outcome models for treated and control rows, then subtract predictions.
expected_strength: Useful when treated and control outcome surfaces differ strongly and both groups have support.

core_idea: Impute treatment effects in each arm and combine them using propensity information.
expected_strength: Often useful when treatment groups are imbalanced or effects are heterogeneous.
